content.thinking: I'm going to hedge step 4 while leaving step 3 as it is, since T20 shows errors continued after the flag was turned off and that point is still open. I'll also consider whether the root cause needs hedging, though the document will already mark it as unverified, so I'll keep it as written.

action_items.item: Turn on io-shop feature flags in stages: a small share of shoppers first, held at each stage while the account page error rate is watched, and rolled back automatically if it rises.

Before any io-shop feature flag can be switched on in production, require tests that run the code paths it enables with the flag on, covering ordinary account states such as a shopper with no purchases this month.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service's share of failed requests rose far above its usual level.
Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. This error first appears in the minute of the onset and does not appear before it.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: none came back from the production change events read for the day before the onset.
Another flag change: the flag provider showed no flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read except this switch of monthly-spend-feature.

causal_chain.step: Account page requests started taking the monthly spend path. An admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}, and from that minute the service's per-request evaluations of the flag read on. Before that they read off, and account pages rendered normally.

A reading of the source that nothing ran suggests that, with the flag on, the account page works out each shopper's average spend per item this month by dividing by the number of purchases they made this month. That would likely raise ZeroDivisionError for shoppers who have bought nothing this month. It is not settled, since the service stayed at the incident's level after the flag was switched off.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary on the account page sent shoppers through a calculation that likely breaks for anyone who has bought nothing this month, so their account pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: monthly-spend-feature went from off to on for nearly all account page requests at the same moment. No staged rollout to a small share of shoppers was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout would have exposed only a small share of shoppers to the failing path while the rise in account page errors showed, which would have kept the harm much smaller.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: Before the flag was switched on in production, no check was seen that ran the account page with monthly-spend-feature on for an ordinary account state such as a shopper with no purchases this month.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Such a check would have hit the ZeroDivisionError before the flag reached shoppers, and the flag would not have been switched on.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person paged when the alert fired would have been on hand to switch the flag back off, or to review the proposed fix, once Argus escalated. That would have shortened the incident.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent formed a candidate tying the failures to the switch-on of monthly-spend-feature and the ZeroDivisionError on account pages, and checked that no deploy was involved.
The Mitigation Agent tried a reversible action first, switching monthly-spend-feature off.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix with tests as a draft pull request, leaving it for a person to review.

went_wrong: When switching the flag off did not seem to help, the flag was put back on. That left on the path the logs tie to the failures, and the harm kept going.
The second investigation came back with the same candidate as the first, which had already been tested for C1 and judged refuted. It offered nothing new to try.

input.root_cause: In src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` integer-divides the account's spend this month by the count of purchases flagged `in_current_month`. That count is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError. `render_spend_summary` calls this function whenever `use_monthly_summary` is true, and the request boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turns the error into a failed account page.
input.still_at_risk: While monthly-spend-feature stayed on, account pages could keep failing for shoppers with no purchases this month, and the same failure could come back any time the flag is switched on before the fix is in.
input.stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. Confirm at the service that io-shop's log lines show requests evaluating the flag off, that the ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py stops appearing, and that the account page error rate returns to its level before the incident.
input.why_it_did_not_help: Find out whether switching monthly-spend-feature off reached io-shop's per-request evaluation of the flag. Read the service's monthly-spend-feature evaluation log lines from the switch-off onward, and how src/io_shop/rollout.py turns the flag into `use_monthly_summary`, for example whether it caches the value. If requests did evaluate the flag off, find out why account page failures continued.
